tier_reason: The README results table (3 September 2026, one run per language, Ryzen 9 5900X at 3.5 GHz) shows Dart 3.13.0 AOT binary trees 0.865 s against C 1.010 s and C++ 1.147 s, and the build table gives the C/C++ flags (gcc/g++ 16.2.0 -O3 -march=native -flto -funroll-loops -ffp-contract=off -s) and the Dart command. The Dart program itself is not in the repository (.gitignore whitelists no *.dart, languages/ has no Dart directory, raw languages/Dart/bench.dart returns 404), so the Dart side cannot be inspected or reproduced and the row cannot reach A.
notes: All numbers check out on the page (Dart 0.865 s, C 1.010 s, C++ 1.147 s; Dart total 20.754 s against C 9.762 s, Fibonacci 8.135 s vs 1.694 s, strings 6.523 s vs 2.132 s). languages/C/bench.c allocates every node with malloc and frees every tree inside the timed loop (make_tree/free_tree), so the win is the harness effect already documented for the OCaml benchLANG binary-trees row (C frees inside the timer, the GC runtime need not collect) plus bump allocation, not Dart codegen; same_algorithm stays unverifiable because the Dart source is missing. Shortcomings: one run, Dart source absent from the repo, 1 of 5 workloads, Dart 2.13x slower overall.

tier_reason: The README tables report Go-only throughput (Ryzen 9 9950X 100KB: 4.03 us/op Rate, 2.10 us/op SSE2, 1.07 us/op AVX2, 685 ns/op AVX512; i7-8850H 100KB: 13.0, 4.05 and 2.31 us/op) with no C timing; no number anywhere in the repository compares against the C xxHash baseline, so the record has no evidence for a win over C.
notes: Record is accurate: _compat.c only prints XXH3 test vectors from the upstream C library (Makefile builds it with plain gcc), compat_test.go checks Go output against those vectors, and internal/compare/compare_test.go benchmarks against cespare/xxhash (Go XXH64), not C. Even a future win would come from the avo-generated SSE2/AVX2/AVX512/NEON assembly accumulators rather than Go codegen. Shortcomings: no C baseline measured (tier D), Go version and flags unstated; metadata checked (BSD-2-Clause, 587 stars, last commit 2026-09-08, not a fork).

tier_reason: Public harness (cbench in nordlow/compiler-benchmark, MIT): bm_Pascal runs 'fpc -Cn -O-' for compile and 'fpc -O- -B -Aas -o<bin>' for build, gcc_clang_op_flags plus bm_C_and_Cxx_using_gcc/clang give gcc/clang -Wall -Wextra and g++/clang++ -Wno-c++11-extensions with -c or -o at the default -O0, DEFAULT_FUNCTION_COUNT and DEFAULT_FUNCTION_DEPTH are 200, the README table names every compiler version and the CPU (AMD Ryzen AI 7 350, Arch Linux). Same tier as the sibling Zig, Odin, C3 and D rows of this suite.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README table (Modern Systems Languages, sample run as of 2026-09): Free Pascal (fpc 3.2.2) Total 138 us/f (137 build + 0.20 run) and Compile 103.6 us/f, against C (gcc-15 15.3.0) 392 Total and 193.8 Compile, C (gcc 16.2.1) 454 Total and 400.1 Compile, C++ (g++-15 15.3.0) 303 Total and 269.6 Compile, C++ (g++ 16.2.1) 486 Total and 372.3 Compile, C++ (clang++ 23.1.1) 236 Total and 82.4 Compile (untemplated rows). Total: about 2.8x faster than gcc-15, 3.3x than gcc 16.2.1 and 1.7x than untemplated clang++ (derived from page data); link-free Compile column: about 1.9x faster than gcc-15, 3.9x than gcc 16.2.1, 2.6x than g++-15 and 3.6x than g++ 16.2.1 (derived from page data). Clang beats Free Pascal: C (clang 23.1.1) 118 Total and 77.9 Compile, C++ (clang++ 23.1.1) 82.4 Compile and 107 Total on the templated variant.
corrections.caveats: The workload is one synthetic 40000-function translation unit of arithmetic with no includes, standard library or optimization, so it does not predict real project build times; at -O2 or -O3 the gcc and clang numbers would be much larger and Free Pascal's -O- row would not be a like-for-like release build. The C compilers are run with -Wall -Wextra (C) and warnings diagnostics that fpc does not get. The Total column adds the run time of the produced binary (0.10 to 0.21 us/f, clang C shows 1.2) and includes linking; the linker used is not stated, Free Pascal is forced to the external GNU assembler by -Aas, while Zig is run with -fno-llvm -fno-lld (own backend and linker) and DMD uses its own backend, so linking work is not uniform across rows. The win holds only against GCC: clang beats Free Pascal in C (118 against 138 Total, 77.9 against 103.6 Compile) and clang++ beats it in the link-free Compile column (82.4 against 103.6) and on the templated Total (107); the 1.7x over clang++ rests on the untemplated Total cell, where clang++'s link step dominates (236 Total against 82.4 Compile). Free Pascal has only an untemplated row. Run-to-run movement on the same machine is large: the README's Conclusions section quotes older numbers than its own table (clang 87 us/f against 118 in the table, gcc 418 to 455 against 392 to 454), and the sibling records' enrichers found the Total cells noisy (20% or more) because the pool runs compilers concurrently on a mixed Zen 5/Zen 5c part, so the Compile column is the more reliable comparison. Parallel pinned workers share caches and memory bandwidth. Both Pascal and Hare sit in the README's 'Modern Systems Languages' table.

notes: All numbers match the README table rows; flags confirmed in cbench (bm_Pascal lines 1864-1897, C_WARN_FLAGS/CXX_WARN_FLAGS lines 398-399, bm_C_and_Cxx_using_gcc/clang). Both sides are unoptimized builds (fpc -O-, gcc/clang default -O0), which is symmetric for a compile-throughput metric. Shortcomings: win over GCC only (clang C and clang++ compile-only are faster), Total cells noisy and include non-uniform linking, synthetic single-file workload; last_commit 2026-10-12 for the GitLab FPC source could not be checked (page did not render activity) and is left as recorded; GitLab shows GPL-2.0-or-later and 75,386 commits.
